brandNames.title: Brand name(s)
brandNames.description: The brands to research. Each name is resolved to its own domain, then traced back to the agencies and freelancers who claim to run its ads. Example: 'My Patriot Supply'.

extraBrandAliases.title: Extra brand aliases
extraBrandAliases.description: Other names a brand answers to — house brands, product lines, the legal entity, social handles. 'My Patriot Supply' also trades as 'Ready Hour'. Applied to every brand in the run.

excludeDomains.title: Never these domains
excludeDomains.description: Extra domains to drop from results and to exclude with -site:, on top of each brand's own domain and the built-in denylist of retailers and publishers.

resolveBrandSites.title: Resolve each brand to its own domain
resolveBrandSites.description: One plain query per brand (not a dork). The domain is not the goal — it is what goes into -site: so the brand's own marketing cannot answer for who runs its ads. Turn off only if you are supplying exclusions yourself.

serpProvider.title: Search provider
serpProvider.description: Where the dorks are run. 'auto' uses the Apify SERP actor when a token is available, and otherwise turns the run off rather than failing halfway through.
serpProvider.sectionDescription: Google blocks datacentre IPs within a handful of advanced-operator queries, so the dorks go through a SERP actor rather than a direct fetch.

serpApifyActorId.title: SERP actor ID
serpApifyActorId.description: The Apify actor that runs the dorks. Any actor taking a multi-line 'queries' input and returning 'organicResults' works.

serpApifyActorInput.title: SERP actor input overrides
serpApifyActorInput.description: Merged last into the SERP actor's input, so any actor-specific option wins — proxy groups, result counts, locale.

serpCountry.title: Search country
serpCountry.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country the searches are issued from.

dorkTiers.title: Dork tiers
dorkTiers.description: Which families of queries to run. 'core' finds most agencies on its own. 'docs' is the one that reaches open Google Docs/Drive/Slides/Canva decks and PDF/PPTX case studies. 'wide' is the long tail — more cost, more noise.

enumTitles: Core — case studies, client rosters, results claims
Docs — Google Docs/Drive/Slides, open Drive folders, Canva, PDF & PPTX decks
Social — LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Medium, Reddit
Wide — wildcards and proximity long tail

dorkTiers.sectionDescription: Queries multiply four axes — the brand, the surface practitioners publish on, the language of claiming credit, and the role words — generated in weighted tiers, with the cap spread across tiers so no one tier eats the budget.

extraDorkSurfaces.title: Extra surfaces
extraDorkSurfaces.description: Raw operator fragments appended to the built-in surface catalogue, e.g. 'site:behance.net' or 'filetype:key'. Each one gets the strongest core recipes.

maxDorkQueries.title: Max dorks per brand
maxDorkQueries.description: Queries are generated in weighted order and the cap is spread across the enabled tiers, so it always contains each tier's strongest queries.

dorkAfterDate.title: Only results after (YYYY-MM-DD)
dorkAfterDate.description: Becomes Google's after: operator. The single best way to ask 'who runs this account NOW' rather than who ran it in 2019.

dorkBeforeDate.title: Only results before (YYYY-MM-DD)
dorkBeforeDate.description: Becomes Google's before: operator. Pair with the after: date to isolate one era of an account.

maxClaimPagesPerBrand.title: Max pages to open per brand
maxClaimPagesPerBrand.description: Hard cap on pages actually fetched and read. This is the real cost control: results are ranked before anything is opened.
maxClaimPagesPerBrand.sectionDescription: A SERP snippet is a claim about a page, not the page. Every surviving result is opened and the brand mention confirmed in the body before anyone is named.

maxHarvestedPages.title: Documents to follow per brand
maxHarvestedPages.description: After opening each dork hit, the actor reads any Google Docs/Drive/Slides/Canva/Notion/Dropbox links off that page and opens those too. This is the main way to reach open Drive material: Google indexes a Drive file only once something crawlable has linked it, and then usually indexes little more than the title. Set to 0 to turn the second pass off.

extraDocumentHosts.title: Extra document hosts to follow
extraDocumentHosts.description: Hosts the second pass should treat as document hosts on top of the built-in list (Google Docs/Drive, Canva, Notion, Dropbox, Airtable, Figma, Miro, Pitch, SlideShare). Use it for a company wiki, a Coda space or a file server, e.g. 'coda.io'.

minClaimScore.title: Minimum claim score
minClaimScore.description: Operators scoring below this are dropped. Raise it for a short, high-confidence list; lower it when a brand returns nothing.

outputFormats.title: Report formats
outputFormats.description: Which reports to write to the key-value store alongside the dataset.

maxConcurrency.title: Max concurrency
maxConcurrency.description: Parallel page fetches. Brands themselves run two at a time whatever this is set to, because each fires its own nested SERP run.

requestTimeoutSecs.title: Request timeout (seconds)
requestTimeoutSecs.description: Per-request timeout when opening a page.

maxRequestRetries.title: Max request retries
maxRequestRetries.description: Retries on a retryable HTTP status or a network failure.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Strongly recommended: agency sites and document hosts both rate-limit datacentre IPs.
